User Guide

Every skill writes to the Data/outputs/ folder with a timestamped filename. Hover the ℹ️ icons for input tips and how to read each output.

AIS Reconcile offline · no LLM direct

Decrypts an AIS (Annual Information Statement) JSON export entirely in-process -- no manual password entry. The entity is resolved from the export's own filename (the portal names it with a masked PAN prefix, e.g. "XXXDE1234X_2025-26_AIS.json"); that masked prefix is matched against entities.yaml's real PANs, and the decrypt password is derived from the resolved entity's PAN plus DOB (Individual) or DOI (HUF). Always runs the AIS-internal check (l1 detail vs l2 aggregate per element, cross-section TDS-credit total). If a 26AS workbook (this repo's own "26AS" skill output) is also supplied, ties out AIS-reported TDS credit against 26AS's tds_deposited at the aggregate, per-quarter, and per-income-category grain. If a GnuCash book for the SAME financial year is also supplied, ties out AIS income (interest/dividend/salary) and TDS credit against what's actually posted in the books -- this is the primary reconciliation, since the books are the taxpayer's own record of truth. A book for the wrong FY still produces a tie-out sheet but the summary carries an impossible-to-miss WARNING banner. Finally, every flagged delta across all three reconciliations is distilled into a set of ADVISORY suggestions for the AIS portal's own feedback mechanism (e.g. "Information is correct", "Information is not fully correct") -- these are for a human to review before acting on the portal; nothing is ever auto-submitted, and confidence is always capped at low/medium, never high.

When to use it. Use once you've downloaded your AIS JSON export from the income-tax portal, to check it against itself and (when available) your 26AS and your GnuCash books before relying on it for filing. The books tie-out is the most useful check if your books are kept current -- it's the only one of the three that can actually tell you the AIS is missing or overstating something, not just disagreeing with another government document.

Inputs

  • Entity (optional) -- fills in the GnuCash book below from the registry (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • AIS JSON export (encrypted, as downloaded from the portal) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: JSON (.json), one export per entity/FY.
  • GnuCash book (optional, must be the SAME FY as the AIS -- enables the books tie-out) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: GnuCash XML book (.gnucash), optionally gzip-compressed.
  • 26AS workbook (optional, from the 26AS skill -- enables the TDS-credit tie-out) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: Excel (.xlsx) with a Part I (TDS) sheet.

How to run

  1. Pick the AIS JSON export.
  2. Optionally supply the matching-FY GnuCash book and/or the entity's 26AS workbook.
  3. Click Run -- it decrypts and reconciles offline in a few seconds.
  4. Open the Excel workbook: Books Reconciliation and 26AS Tie-out sheets first, then Feedback Suggestions.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-ais-reconciliation.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-ais-reconciliation.xlsxℹ️ — Summary, Books Reconciliation (if a book was supplied), one sheet per AIS section, Flags, 26AS Tie-out (if a workbook was supplied), and Feedback Suggestions (advisory only).

Tips

The Feedback Suggestions sheet is a starting point for the AIS portal's own feedback form, not something to paste in verbatim -- read the Rationale column and confirm each suggestion against the underlying document before acting on the portal. Confidence is deliberately capped at "low"/"medium": nothing here is ever certain enough to call "high" without a human's own review.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
"ERROR: no entity ... has a PAN matching the masked prefix".Add or correct the entity's pan in entities.yaml, or confirm the AIS filename wasn't renamed away from the portal's own masked-PAN_FY_... convention.
"ERROR: could not decrypt ...".The resolved entity's dob/doi in entities.yaml doesn't match what the portal used to encrypt this export -- double-check the date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) on file.
WARNING about the GnuCash book having no transactions in the AIS's FY.You picked the wrong .gnucash book (or the wrong-year one) -- re-run with the book covering the same financial year as the AIS export.

Bank of Baroda offline · no LLM direct

Turns one or more Bank of Baroda transaction-statement PDFs into a single flat CSV — one row per transaction. Runs fully offline (no LLM, no internet) and correctly stitches tables that overflow across pages without repeating the column header, so a transaction that wraps from the bottom of one page to the top of the next is captured as a single clean row.

When to use it. Use this when you have BoB account statements as PDFs and want them as a tidy CSV you can open in Excel, reconcile, or feed into the Banks "Convert to GnuCash" pipeline (choose "Bank of Baroda" there to do extraction + account mapping in one step instead). This skill is extraction only — it does not categorise or assign accounts.

Inputs

  • Bank of Baroda statement PDF(s) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: PDF (.pdf) — one or many, in any order.

How to run

  1. Click the input and pick one or more Bank of Baroda statement PDFs.
  2. Click Run — it processes offline in a few seconds.
  3. Download the CSV, or open it from the outputs folder (see below).

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-BoB.csv
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-BoB.csvℹ️ — One row per transaction with columns: Date, Particulars, Cheque No., Withdrawals, Deposits, Balance. Rows are in statement order; multi-page transactions are merged so no row is split.

Tips

The running balance carries straight from the statement — if the final Balance matches your passbook, the extraction tied out. Re-run with more PDFs to append additional periods (each run writes a new timestamped file). Columns are kept verbatim from the statement so amounts are not rounded or reformatted.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
The output CSV is empty or has very few rows.The PDF is probably a scanned image, not a text PDF. Re-download the original statement from BoB net-banking, or run it through an OCR step first. This skill does not OCR.
Run fails saying the PDF could not be opened.The PDF is password-protected. Unlock it (open in a viewer, print/save as a new unprotected PDF) and try again.
Closing balance in the CSV does not match my passbook.Check you included every page/period and that no statement was selected twice. Each run lists rows in statement order so you can scan for a gap.

CSV Data Analyzer needs LLM endpoint agent

Ask a plain-English question about any CSV and get a written answer with the numbers worked out. The agent loads the file, reasons over the rows, and returns a short Markdown report.

When to use it. Use this for quick, ad-hoc analysis ("average revenue by region?", "which month had the most refunds?") without writing spreadsheet formulas. For a formatted spreadsheet deliverable, use Excel directly instead.

Inputs

  • CSV file (required) ℹ️
    accepts: CSV (.csv) with a header row.
  • Question about this data (e.g. 'What is the average revenue by region?') (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Free text.

How to run

  1. Pick your CSV file.
  2. Type your question.
  3. Click Run and read (or download) the Markdown answer.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-analysis.md
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-analysis.mdℹ️ — A Markdown write-up answering your question, including the figures the agent computed.

Tips

Treat the answer as a first pass — spot-check any number that drives a decision, since the model reasons over the data rather than running fixed formulas.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Run errors mentioning the endpoint / model.This skill needs an LLM. Start Ollama or configure an endpoint in Settings.
Answer seems to ignore part of the data.Large CSVs may be sampled; narrow the file or the question and re-run.

Convert offline · no LLM direct

Converts a Form 26AS PDF (the TRACES Annual Tax Statement) into a structured Excel workbook with one sheet per Part (Part I through Part X). The two parts that carry your tax credits are laid out in full as sortable tables with inline per-party sub-totals: Part I (TDS) and Part VI (TCS). The remaining parts get their column headers so the workbook is predictable. Note that a modern 26AS carries NO advance tax or self-assessment tax — those were dropped from Part C in AY 2023-24 and now live only in the AIS. Runs fully offline.

When to use it. Use this when you have your 26AS PDF from the TRACES portal and want it as Excel to review or reconcile against your ITR. To then post the TDS into GnuCash as journal entries, run "26AS Journal" on the workbook this produces. Do not use it for AIS or TIS — those are different documents.

Inputs

  • Form 26AS PDF (required) ℹ️
    accepts: PDF (.pdf) — a single TRACES-issued 26AS.

How to run

  1. Pick your 26AS PDF.
  2. Click Run — it processes offline in a few seconds.
  3. Open the Excel workbook and use the per-Part sheets.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-26AS.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-26AS.xlsxℹ️ — One worksheet per Part (I–X). Each transaction is a flat row; each deductor block ends with a sub-total row so you can tie figures back to the source statement without re-adding them.

Tips

Amounts are kept verbatim from the statement (no rounding). Cross-check the Part I TDS total against the TDS you are claiming in your return, and the Part VI TCS total too — TCS on a foreign tour package or LRS remittance is a credit like any other, and leaving it out understates your refund.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Sheets are empty or the text is garbled.The PDF is a scan. Re-download the text 26AS from TRACES; this skill does not OCR.
Columns look wrong / parts are missing.The file is likely an AIS or TIS, not a 26AS. Use the correct 26AS PDF.

Convert offline · no LLM direct

Part I of the KR Choksey → GnuCash flow. Simplifies the annual KR Choksey broker ledger-statement PDF into a clean, tied-out "Simplified Ledger" Excel workbook. Runs fully offline (deterministic, no LLM).

When to use it. Run this first of the three KRChoksey sub-tabs. Its workbook is the input to "Reconcile" (Part II), which in turn feeds "Convert to GnuCash" (Part III).

Inputs

  • KR Choksey Ledger Statement PDF (required) ℹ️
    accepts: PDF (.pdf) — the ledger statement.
  • PDF password (account holder's PAN) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Text — the account holder's PAN.

How to run

  1. Select the KR Choksey ledger statement PDF.
  2. Enter the PDF password (the account holder's PAN).
  3. Click Run and download the Simplified Ledger workbook.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-KRC-Ledger.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-KRC-Ledger.xlsxℹ️ — The Simplified Ledger: the annual statement re-laid as a clean, tied-out workbook. This is the file you pick in the Reconcile (Part II) tab.

Tips

Run the three KRChoksey tabs in order — Convert, then Reconcile, then Convert to GnuCash. Each later tab picks this output from a dropdown of prior runs.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Run fails opening the PDF.Check the password is the correct PAN. Ensure qpdf is available in source mode.
Rows look incomplete.Confirm you selected the full annual ledger statement, not a single contract note.

Convert to GnuCash needs LLM endpoint agent

Builds GnuCash journal entries from a 26AS workbook plus your GnuCash book. It reads Part I (TDS) and Part VI (TCS), matches each deductor to one of your accounts (deterministic fuzzy match first, LLM fallback for the hard cases), and writes a balanced journal CSV ready to import. TCS entries debit your TCS account and credit Drawings — only the tax moves, since the spend it was collected on is already in your books.

When to use it. Use this after "26AS Convert", when you want the TDS and TCS recorded in GnuCash as journal entries instead of typing each one by hand. Getting TCS into the book matters: it is a credit against your tax, and if it never reaches the books your return understates the refund due.

Inputs

  • Entity (optional) -- fills in the GnuCash book below from the registry (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • 26AS workbook (Convert output) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Excel (.xlsx) matching *-26AS.xlsx.
  • GnuCash file (required) ℹ️
    accepts: GnuCash file (.gnucash).

How to run

  1. Pick the 26AS workbook from the dropdown of prior outputs.
  2. Select your .gnucash book (make sure GnuCash has it closed).
  3. Click Run; review any deductors flagged as unmatched.
  4. Import the CSV into GnuCash: File > Import > Import Transactions from CSV.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-tds-journals.csv
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-tds-journals.csvℹ️ — One balanced journal transaction per TDS entry (every transaction's amounts sum to zero), debiting the TDS receivable / asset account and crediting the income account, ready for GnuCash CSV import.
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-tds-journals-partI.csvℹ️ — Only written when the 26AS has 15G/15H (Part II) entries: the same journal with every 15G/15H transaction dropped whole. Import this instead of the full journal if you post 15G/15H entries by hand in GnuCash yourself, so the Interest-on-FD reclassification is not double-booked. Regenerated on every save from the Review screen, so it can never go stale.

Tips

Entries whose deductor could not be matched to an account are flagged so you can fix the account name in your book (or add the missing account) and re-run.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Run errors mentioning the endpoint / model.This skill uses an LLM for fallback matching. Start Ollama (or set an endpoint in Settings).
A deductor was assigned the wrong account.Rename/add the account in GnuCash so its name is closer to the deductor, then re-run.

Convert to GnuCash needs LLM endpoint agent

The one-click, end-to-end importer: upload a raw bank statement and your GnuCash book and get back a GnuCash-ready, account-mapped CSV — no intermediate steps. It chains bank extraction, conversion to canonical format, and account mapping for you. HDFC statements are handled fully deterministically (no LLM) across all four input shapes it accepts — normal PDF, password-protected PDF, XLS/XLSX exports, and CSV exports — including automatic OCR fallback if a PDF's text layer is garbled.

When to use it. Use this when your goal is to get transactions into GnuCash. Use the individual bank skills (BoB, HDFC, etc.) instead only when you want the extracted CSV without account mapping.

Inputs

  • Entity (optional) -- fills in the GnuCash book below from the registry (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • Bank (required) ℹ️
    accepts: One of: ICICI, Bank of Baroda, HSBC, HDFC, Kotak, Other Bank (CSV).
  • Statement file(s) — XLS for ICICI; PDF(s) for BoB / HSBC / Kotak; CSV or XLS/XLSX for HDFC / Other (required) ℹ️
    accepts: XLS for ICICI; PDF(s) for BoB / HSBC / Kotak; CSV or XLS/XLSX for HDFC / Other.
  • GnuCash book (.gnucash) — must be closed in GnuCash (required) ℹ️
    accepts: GnuCash file (.gnucash).
  • PDF password (HDFC only — if the statement PDF is password-protected, for HDFC often the Cust ID) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: The statement's open password — for HDFC this is often the Cust ID.

How to run

  1. Pick the entity (optional) — this fills in the GnuCash book for you.
  2. Choose the bank.
  3. Upload the matching statement file(s).
  4. Select your .gnucash book (closed in GnuCash), unless the entity already filled it in.
  5. Click Run, then import the resulting CSV via File > Import in GnuCash.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-GnuCash_import_ready.csv
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-GnuCash_import_ready.csvℹ️ — The statement converted to canonical columns AND mapped to your GnuCash accounts (based on your book's history), ready to import directly — no manual categorising.

Tips

Account mapping learns from your existing GnuCash history, so the more you have categorised before, the better the auto-mapping. Review a few rows after import the first time. For HDFC, prefer the plain PDF, XLS/XLSX, or CSV export over a password-protected PDF when you have the choice — extraction is equally deterministic either way, but if HDFC ever hands you a PDF whose text layer is garbled (rare, seen on some re-downloaded statements), the skill auto-detects it and falls back to OCR, which is typically ~90%+ accurate rather than exact; re-check the running/closing balance in that case.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Run errors mentioning the endpoint / model.Mapping (and 'Other Bank' normalisation) uses an LLM. Start Ollama or set an endpoint in Settings.
Extraction fails immediately.The file type probably doesn't match the chosen bank (e.g. a PDF selected for ICICI). Re-check both.
Some rows mapped to the wrong account.Fix them in GnuCash after import; future runs learn from the correction.

Convert to GnuCash offline · no LLM direct

Part III of the KR Choksey → GnuCash flow. Converts the Part II Bills workbook into importable GnuCash multi-split CSVs — Purchase, SLBM and Sale — using FIFO cost basis and the long-term holding threshold from your .gnucash book and an editable config in Data/settings/. Runs fully offline.

When to use it. Run this last of the three KRChoksey tabs, after Reconcile (Part II). It produces the CSVs you import into GnuCash.

Inputs

  • Entity (optional) -- fills in the GnuCash book below from the registry (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • Part II Bills workbook (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Excel (.xlsx) matching *-KRC-Bills-Recon.xlsx.
  • GnuCash book (.gnucash) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: GnuCash file (.gnucash).

How to run

  1. Pick the Part II Bills workbook from the dropdown.
  2. Select your .gnucash book (closed in GnuCash).
  3. Click Run, then open the output folder.
  4. Import each CSV into GnuCash (File > Import > Import Transactions from CSV).

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-KRC-GnuCash/
  • Purchase.csvℹ️ — One transaction per purchase: Dr the security account (with share quantity), Cr the KR Choksey broker account, for the net/bill amount.
  • SLBM.csvℹ️ — One transaction per SLBM bill: Dr KR Choksey broker, Cr Income from SLBS (net lending proceeds, offered to tax as income).
  • Sale.csvℹ️ — Multi-split per sale: Dr broker (proceeds), Cr security at FIFO cost basis (negative shares), Cr Long/Short Term Capital Gain (a loss appears as a debit).
  • Review.csvℹ️ — Only created when something needs attention — an unmatched security name, or a sale with insufficient FIFO lots.

Tips

Every transaction's Amount column sums to zero, so each imports as a balanced GnuCash transaction. The long-term threshold and account paths come from your book plus the editable config in Data/settings/.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
A Review.csv appears.Open it: either a security name didn't match an account (add/rename it) or a sale lacked enough FIFO lots (check earlier purchases were imported).
Capital gain looks wrong.Confirm the holding-period threshold and account paths in Data/settings/ match your setup.

Coverage Gap Detector offline · no LLM direct

This codebase has no ledger of which statements were ever imported, so this skill infers likely-missing months a different way: for every bank (BANK/ASSET) and credit-card (LIABILITY/CREDIT) account in the book(s) you select, it buckets that account's own transactions by calendar month across its active window (first transaction to FY-end or today, whichever is earlier) and reports every zero-transaction month it finds. Each zero month is graded HIGH or LOW confidence from that account's own median monthly transaction count (shown alongside so the grading is auditable) -- never silently suppressed. Months after an account's LAST transaction get their own prominent trailing-gap flag, since that usually means the most recent statement was never imported. A zero month that falls on the book's own FY-boundary (its first or last calendar month) is cross-checked against the adjacent FY's registered book for the same entity/account before being reported, since postings are sometimes filed on the wrong side of a year rollover by mistake.

When to use it. Run periodically (e.g. monthly, or before filing) to catch a bank or credit-card statement that was never imported into GnuCash -- something the per-statement opening-balance check in the GnuCash Pipeline skill cannot see, because it only ever compares one statement against one account and has nothing to compare against when a whole month's statement is simply missing.

Inputs

  • Entities (pick one or more -- fills their registered books below) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One or more entities from the Entities tab. Optional -- you can Browse to the books instead.
  • GnuCash books (.gnucash) -- one or more; all must be closed in GnuCash (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Paths to GnuCash files (.gnucash) -- filled from the entity picker above, or added with Browse.

How to run

  1. Pick the entities to scan -- their registered books fill in automatically.
  2. Browse to any book that did not fill in (closed in GnuCash).
  3. Click Run and download the coverage gap report.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Coverage-Gaps.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Coverage-Gaps.xlsxℹ️ — Gaps sheet (one row per suspected gap month: entity, book, account, account class, month, HIGH/LOW confidence, the account's own median, and a TRAILING flag for gaps since the last transaction) and a Summary sheet (one row per in-scope account: first/last transaction, active-window end, median, confidence, and gap counts).

Tips

Start with the TRAILING rows in the Gaps sheet -- those are gaps since an account's most recent transaction and are the most likely to mean a statement still needs importing. A LOW-confidence gap on a quiet account (e.g. a savings account paid quarterly interest) is often expected -- check the account's own median in the Summary sheet before chasing it.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
An account I expect to see is missing from both sheets.Accounts with NO transactions at all in the book are not reported -- there is nothing to grade a cadence against. Placeholder/hidden accounts are also excluded, same as elsewhere in the GnuCash skills.
A gap I know about did not show up.It may have been suppressed because the adjacent FY's registered book has a transaction for the same account in that exact month -- a sign it was filed on the wrong side of the year rollover rather than missing. Check the Summary sheet's 'FY-Boundary Suppressed' column.

Credit Card — Sort PDFs offline · no LLM direct

Takes a messy folder of credit-card statements and organises it: it pulls PDF attachments out of Outlook .msg emails, decrypts password-protected PDFs (via qpdf), and sorts everything by bank/issuer into a clean folder tree. Runs fully offline.

When to use it. Use this as the first step when you have a pile of statement emails and PDFs from several cards. Once sorted, run "CC Transactions" on the decrypted folder to extract the actual transactions.

Inputs

  • Input folder (MSG files and/or PDFs) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: A folder of .msg and/or .pdf files.
  • PDF password(s), comma-separated (or leave blank for auto-detect) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: Text — one password, or several comma-separated. Optional.

How to run

  1. Select the folder holding your statement emails / PDFs.
  2. Optionally enter PDF password(s); leave blank to auto-detect.
  3. Click Run, then open the output folder.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-CC-Sort/
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-CC-Sort/ (a folder)ℹ️ — Contains Decrypted_PDFs_Correct/ — the unlocked, de-duplicated PDFs to feed into CC Transactions — alongside copies sorted by issuer. Use the "Open output folder" button to browse it.

Tips

This step never reads transaction amounts; it only unlocks and organises. The folder it produces is the exact input the CC Transactions skill expects.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
A PDF stays locked / is skipped.Enter its password in the password box (comma-separate multiple) and re-run.
Source-mode run fails on decryption.qpdf must be on PATH in source mode; the frozen build bundles it.

Credit Card — Transactions offline · no LLM direct

Reads the organised credit-card PDFs from the CC Sort step and extracts every transaction table into one consolidated Excel workbook — one row per transaction across all cards. Runs fully offline.

When to use it. Use this as the second step, right after "CC Sort". It expects the decrypted, sorted folder that CC Sort produced, not raw statement files.

Inputs

  • Organized PDFs folder (Decrypted_PDFs_Correct/ from CC Sort) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: A folder of decrypted statement PDFs.

How to run

  1. Run CC Sort first if you have not already.
  2. Select the Decrypted_PDFs_Correct/ folder.
  3. Click Run and download the Excel.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-CC-Transactions.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-CC-Transactions.xlsxℹ️ — One consolidated sheet of transactions across all sorted statements, with date, description and amount columns extracted from each card's table.

Tips

Because the PDFs are already grouped by issuer, the consolidated sheet keeps cards together — handy for per-card filtering in Excel.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Few or no transactions extracted.You probably pointed at the wrong folder. Use Decrypted_PDFs_Correct/ from CC Sort.

Document Summarizer needs LLM endpoint direct

Summarises any PDF or text file into a concise Markdown summary using your configured LLM.

When to use it. Use this for a quick readable summary of a document — a report, a long text file, a contract. For asking specific questions of tabular data, use CSV Data Analyzer instead.

Inputs

  • Document (PDF or text file) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: PDF (.pdf) or text (.txt, .md, .csv, .log, .json, .xml, .html) — one file.

How to run

  1. Pick the document.
  2. Click Run.
  3. Read or download the Markdown summary.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-summary.md
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-summary.mdℹ️ — A Markdown summary capturing the document's main points.

Tips

Very long documents may be condensed heavily — for a specific section, point the skill at just that text.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Run errors mentioning the endpoint / model.This skill needs an LLM. Start Ollama or set an endpoint in Settings.
Summary is thin or generic.The PDF may be a scan with no text layer. Use a text-based document.

HDFC offline · no LLM direct

Converts HDFC statements — digital PDF, password-protected PDF, scanned/garbled-text PDF, net-banking XLS/XLSX, or CSV export — into a GnuCash-ready canonical CSV. All four shapes are parsed deterministically (no LLM). A garbled/unusable PDF text layer (custom font encoding) is auto-detected and routed to OCR with Tesseract automatically. Runs offline.

When to use it. Use this to get a clean, consistently-columned CSV from any HDFC statement format. To also map the rows to GnuCash accounts in one step, use the GnuCash Import skill and choose HDFC instead.

Inputs

  • HDFC statement (PDF, XLS, XLSX, or CSV) (required) ℹ️

  • PDF password (only if the statement PDF is password-protected — for HDFC often the Cust ID) (optional) ℹ️

How to run

  1. Pick your HDFC statement file (XLS/XLSX preferred, PDF and CSV also work).
  2. If the PDF is password-protected, enter its password.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-HDFC_canonical.csv
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-HDFC_canonical.csvℹ️ — The statement in canonical columns (date, description, debit/credit, balance) — the same shape every bank skill emits, so it feeds straight into the GnuCash account-mapping pipeline.

Prefer the net-banking XLS/XLSX export when you have the choice — it skips OCR entirely and is exact. All four input shapes should produce the same rows and balances for the same statement period.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
A scanned or font-garbled PDF produces poor or missing rows.Use the XLS/XLSX/CSV export instead if available. If you only have a PDF, use the bank's original (net-banking download) PDF rather than a derived/re-printed one — printing-to-PDF strips the digital text layer and forces lower-fidelity OCR even when the original would have parsed directly. Ensure Tesseract is available in source mode; OCR fidelity depends on scan quality.
'PDF is password-protected' error.Enter the statement's password in the pdf_password field — for HDFC this is often the account Cust ID.
Columns do not look canonical.Confirm the file is a real HDFC statement; other banks have their own skills.

ITR Workbook offline · no LLM direct

Builds a formula-driven Indian ITR input workbook from a GnuCash "Balance Sheet (eguile)" HTML export (P&L embedded via Retained Earnings). Always runs the full identity/reconciliation check suite (Imbalance == 0, Assets == Equity+Trading+Liabilities+Retained Earnings, every subtotal == sum of its children). Pick the Entity and Assessment Year from the dropdowns (populated from Data/itr/entities.yaml and Data/itr/rules/tax_rules_*.yaml); the selected AY must match the income year inferred from the HTML's own as-of date, or the run hard-fails before any schedule build is attempted. If a matching .gnucash book is also supplied, runs a book<->HTML cross-check per income/expense account. If an entity mapping is also supplied, resolves every leaf to a tag (nearest-ancestor); any unmapped account sets the run status to BLOCKED-FOR-REVIEW and writes a proposed-mappings snippet (with an LLM suggestion per account when an endpoint is configured) ready to paste into the mapping file. If a Form 16 PDF is also supplied, parses its Part B/Annexure-I salary computation, prints the employer TAN, the 115BAC(1A) opt-out election, and the form's own internal consistency checks; an encrypted PDF is decrypted automatically using the selected entity's PAN on file (no need to re-type it). When a mapping is also available, additionally cross-checks 17(1) gross salary against SALARY_GROSS and net tax payable against TAXPAID_TDS_SALARY. If a 26AS workbook is also supplied, ties out reported TDS by quarter and feeds the 234C dividend-quarter buckets. If a foreign broker consolidated tax report is also supplied, parses Schedule FA (foreign assets, one row per acquisition lot), Schedule FSI (foreign-sourced income), Form 67 (foreign tax credit claim), and Schedule TR (tax relief summary), and writes them as their own labelled sheets; the book-derived AL_FOREIGN roll-up keeps running unchanged as an independent, separately labelled cross-check beneath, never merged into the parsed figures. Absent this input, Schedule FA output is unchanged from before. The Regime dropdown overrides the entity's configured regime for this run only (leave blank to use the entity's default for the selected AY). Marginal relief, surcharge caps, age-linked slabs/deductions, and every rate/cap/section referenced in the output are driven entirely from the Rules config for the selected year — nothing is hardcoded.

When to use it. Use once book, mapping, and (optionally) Form 16 / 26AS inputs are ready for an entity and assessment year, to produce the standardized ITR input workbook for review or handoff to a CA. An unmapped account or a selected-AY/HTML-year mismatch blocks the run rather than silently misstating income.

Inputs

  • Balance Sheet (eguile) HTML (required) ℹ️
    accepts: HTML (.html), one file per entity.
  • Entity (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • Assessment Year (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the years found under Data/itr/rules/, via dropdown.
  • Regime (blank = use the entity's configured regime) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: "new", "old", or blank to use the entity's configured regime.
  • GnuCash book (optional, enables CG lots + dividend quarters) (optional)
    accepts: .gnucash
  • Entity mapping (optional, enables the account-tag resolution + BLOCKED-FOR-REVIEW check) (optional)
    accepts: .yaml
  • Form 16 PDF (optional, fills the Salary sheet; password auto-derived from the selected entity's PAN if encrypted) (optional)
    accepts: .pdf, .PDF
  • 26AS workbook (optional, feeds TDS tie-out + 234C quarters) (optional)
    accepts: .xlsx
  • Foreign broker consolidated tax report (optional, fills Schedule FA/FSI/Form 67/Schedule TR) (optional)
    accepts: .xlsx

How to run

  1. Pick the Balance Sheet (eguile) HTML export.
  2. Select the Entity and Assessment Year from the dropdowns.
  3. Optionally supply the GnuCash book, entity mapping, Form 16 PDF, 26AS workbook, and/or a foreign broker consolidated tax report.
  4. Click Run to build the workbook and print the verification summary.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-ITR.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-ITR.xlsxℹ️ — The full ITR input workbook, or a stub with an ERROR summary if the run was blocked.

Tips

book_file runs the book<->HTML cross-check. mapping_file runs the account-tag resolution; an unmapped account blocks the run and emits a proposed-mappings snippet next to the output file. form16_pdf runs the salary parse + internal consistency checks, plus the Book<->Form16 cross-checks when mapping_file is also supplied; the decryption password is auto-derived from the selected entity's PAN. as26_workbook ties out TDS by quarter and feeds 234C dividend-quarter bucketing. foreign_report_xlsx fills Schedule FA/FSI/Form 67/Schedule TR from the broker's own report; any cell the source left as a placeholder or instructional prose is rendered as an explicit flagged string, never left blank or coerced to zero. If the Entity/Assessment Year dropdowns look stale after editing entities.yaml or the rules config, use the refresh button beside them.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
"file truncated -- re-export" error.The HTML export is missing its trailing Imbalance Amount row. Re-export from GnuCash.
"ERROR: selected Assessment Year does not match" and only a stub workbook is produced.Pick the Assessment Year that matches the uploaded HTML's as-of date, or upload the HTML for the selected year, then run again.

Inter-entity Matrix offline · no LLM direct

An optional roll-up over the pairwise Inter-entity Reconcile: it reconciles every unordered pair among the books you select and rolls them into one workbook -- a colour-coded owner-by-owner difference grid, a per-pair summary, and one consolidated exceptions list. Same deterministic engine, read-only on your books.

  • Custom end date (YYYY-MM-DD) -- only for 'Custom date range' (optional) ℹ️

  2. Browse to any book that did not fill in (closed in GnuCash).

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Inter-entity-Matrix.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Inter-entity-Matrix.xlsxℹ️ — Matrix sheet (owner-by-owner difference grid, green ties / red out of balance / grey n/a), Pairs sheet (balances and counts per pair), and All Exceptions (every unmatched item across all pairs with the best probable posting found in the other book).

Tips

Start from the Matrix grid: any red cell is a pair to open. The All Exceptions sheet is the single actionable to-do list across the whole family.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
A pair shows 'n/a'.Those two books do not each keep an account named for the other. That is normal for people who do not transact.

Inter-entity Reconcile offline · no LLM direct

Reconciles the contra accounts two people keep for each other across their two GnuCash books. It matches the current financial year's movements, carries the opening balance forward, and for every unmatched item searches the other book for a probable mis-posting -- then writes an Excel reconciliation statement. Fully offline and deterministic (no LLM); read-only on your books.

When to use it. Run at year-end (or before filing) to confirm that what one person's book shows as due to/from the other agrees with the other person's book -- and to catch entries one side recorded that the other missed or mis-posted.

Inputs

  • First entity (optional) -- fills in the first GnuCash book below from the registry (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • First person's GnuCash book (.gnucash) -- must be closed in GnuCash (required) ℹ️
    accepts: GnuCash file (.gnucash).
  • Second entity (optional) -- fills in the second GnuCash book below from the registry (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • Second person's GnuCash book (.gnucash) -- must be closed in GnuCash (required) ℹ️
    accepts: GnuCash file (.gnucash).
  • Reconciliation period (Indian FY = 1 Apr to 31 Mar) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: A FY, a calendar year, Auto, or a custom date range.
  • Custom start date (YYYY-MM-DD) -- only for 'Custom date range' (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: YYYY-MM-DD.
  • Custom end date (YYYY-MM-DD) -- only for 'Custom date range' (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: YYYY-MM-DD.
  • Date tolerance in days for matching in-transit items (default 7) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: A whole number of days. Default 7.

How to run

  1. Pick both people's .gnucash books (closed in GnuCash).
  2. Choose the reconciliation period (or leave on Auto).
  3. Optionally adjust the date tolerance.
  4. Click Run and download the reconciliation workbook.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Inter-entity-Recon.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Inter-entity-Recon.xlsxℹ️ — The reconciliation statement: a Summary (opening, movements, closing, and the balance difference), a Matched sheet pairing both books' entries, and an Exceptions sheet per side listing unmatched items with probable mis-postings found in the other book.

Tips

If the balance ties but exceptions remain, those items usually net to zero (a give-and-take one side recorded and the other did not) -- still worth fixing. Descriptions mentioning 'HUF' against an individual's contra account signal an entry that belongs in the HUF book instead.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
No contra account found.The other person's name must appear in an account name in each book. Rename the account to include their name, then re-run.
An item shows 'No candidate found in the other book'.The other person genuinely never recorded it, OR it belongs to a related entity (e.g. an HUF) whose book was not the one you loaded.
Too many unmatched items that clearly correspond.Increase the date tolerance -- the payments are landing in the other book more than a week apart.

Kotak offline · no LLM direct

Turns a Kotak Mahindra Bank savings-account transaction-statement PDF into a flat CSV — one row per transaction. Runs fully offline (no LLM, no internet) and reads the statement's ruled/bordered table structure directly, so a table that overflows from one page to the next (without repeating the column header) is still captured correctly, and the trailing abbreviation-legend page is excluded rather than mistaken for transaction rows.

When to use it. Use this when you have a Kotak savings-account statement as a PDF and want it as a tidy CSV you can open in Excel, reconcile, or feed into the Banks "Convert to GnuCash" pipeline (choose "Kotak" there to do extraction + account mapping in one step instead). This skill is extraction only — it does not categorise or assign accounts.

Inputs

  • Kotak statement PDF (required) ℹ️
    accepts: PDF (.pdf) — one statement per run.

How to run

  1. Click the input and pick a Kotak statement PDF.
  2. Click Run — it processes offline in a few seconds.
  3. Download the CSV, or open it from the outputs folder (see below).

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Kotak.csv
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-Kotak.csvℹ️ — One row per transaction with columns: #, Date, Description, Chq/Ref. No., Withdrawal, Deposit, Balance. Rows are in statement order; the "Opening Balance" front-matter row and the trailing abbreviation-legend page are both excluded from the CSV.

Tips

The running balance carries straight from the statement — if the final Balance matches your passbook, the extraction tied out. Sweep-in/sweep-out transfers to a linked Fixed Deposit are kept as real transactions, not filtered out. Columns are kept verbatim from the statement so amounts are not rounded or reformatted.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
The output CSV is empty or has very few rows.The PDF is probably a scanned image, not a text PDF. Re-download the original statement from Kotak net-banking, or run it through an OCR step first. This skill does not OCR.
Run fails saying the PDF could not be opened.The PDF is password-protected. Unlock it (open in a viewer, print/save as a new unprotected PDF) and try again.
Closing balance in the CSV does not match my passbook.Check the statement's last page — the abbreviation legend on that page is intentionally excluded, but if any real transaction rows sit above it, make sure the whole document (all pages) was included when you selected the PDF.

MF Capital Gain Statement offline · no LLM direct

Reads KFintech's "Capital Gain / Loss Statement" -- an RTA-issued, password-protected .xlsx workbook that already lists every acquisition matched against its disposal, with the RTA's own short-term/long-term gain figures and grandfathered cost values -- and turns it into a matched-lots ledger, a per-scheme summary, a s.234C period-wise summary (the five advance-tax instalment buckets), and a three-way reconciliation across the statement's own Trasaction_Details, Scheme_Level_Summary, and Summary sheets. This is NOT the raw, transaction-wise CAS (Consolidated Account Statement) -- the RTA has already done the buy/sell matching here, so no FIFO reconstruction is performed. Only the figures the statement itself supplies are emitted; no tax rate, slab, exemption, or indexation computation is done -- that is left to the ITR Workbook skill's own tax-rules config. Grandfathered cost values (for holdings bought before 2018-02-01) are carried through exactly as KFintech supplies them, since the RTA has already applied the FMV as of 31-Jan-2018 -- this skill never needs and never looks up a separate FMV source for this statement.

When to use it. Use this after receiving your KFintech Capital Gain / Loss Statement (typically requested/downloaded per financial year) for mutual funds serviced by KFintech, when you need a clean realised-capital-gains feed to review or feed manually into the ITR Workbook. This skill does NOT cover CAMS-serviced funds -- CAMS issues its own, differently-shaped Capital Gain statement, which this skill does not yet support. GnuCash books in this codebase hold mutual funds only as cash transfers to the AMC, so there is no commodity-lot data inside GnuCash for capital gains to be derived from automatically.

Inputs

  • KFintech Capital Gain / Loss Statement (.xlsx) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: .xlsx (.pdf is not supported -- see troubleshooting below).
  • Statement password (required) ℹ️
    accepts: The statement's open password (KFintech's own delivery convention -- check the email/portal you got the file from).

How to run

  1. Download your KFintech Capital Gain / Loss Statement (.xlsx) from KFintech's portal or email delivery.
  2. Pick the .xlsx file and enter its password.
  3. Click Run.
  4. Download the workbook and review the Reconciliation and Exceptions sheets first.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-MF-CAS.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-MF-CAS.xlsxℹ️ — Five sheets: MatchedLots (every RTA-matched acquisition/outflow/ gain row, as-is), SchemeSummary (Scheme_Level_Summary, as given), PeriodSummary (the five s.234C bucket figures per section from both Summary sheets), Reconciliation (the three-way agree/variance/cannot-reconcile result per gain category), and Exceptions (every category that did not agree or could not be reconciled, collected in one place).
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-MF-CAS_matched_lots.csvℹ️ — CSV sibling of the MatchedLots sheet.

Tips

Start with the Reconciliation sheet -- it shows, per gain category (Short Term, Long Term With Indexation, Long Term Without Indexation), whether the statement's own Trasaction_Details row sum, its Scheme_Level_Summary total, and its Summary sheet total all agree. A "CANNOT RECONCILE" result means one of those three figures was not present in this particular workbook -- it is reported explicitly rather than silently treated as a match.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
'xlsx is password-protected — supply the statement password (the statement's own open password, as supplied by KFintech).' error.Enter the statement's own open password, as supplied by KFintech.
This skill no longer accepts a PDF.KFintech issues the Capital Gain / Loss Statement as an encrypted .xlsx workbook, not a PDF. Depository *_TXN.pdf files and PDF parsing of the CG statement are out of scope for this skill.
'This workbook does not look like a KFintech Capital Gain / Loss Statement.'Confirm the file is KFintech's own Capital Gain / Loss Statement export (sheets: Summary - Equity, Summary - NonEquity, Scheme_Level_Summary, Trasaction_Details), not a CAMS statement or a different KFintech report.
A reconciliation category shows VARIANCE.The three figures for that gain category did not agree within tolerance. Check the Reconciliation sheet's Note column for the exact numbers, and re-check the source statement for a corporate action this skill does not model.

Parser Generator needs LLM endpoint agent

A developer-time tool that creates or repairs the project's embedded deterministic parsers (src/agents/skill_<X>/scripts/parse_<format>.py). It is template-based: the model may only fill format-specific blanks (column ranges, regexes, row-boundary and skip rules); the balance oracle and the 0/1/2 exit contract are off-limits. Every result must pass the quality gate (validate -> tie-out exit 0) before you commit it.

When to use it. Use "Fix a failing parser" when a statement format changed and a parser's tie-out fails (the oracle exits 2). Use "Create a new parser" to scaffold one for a new format from the shared template. This is for maintainers, not end-of-day statement processing. See docs/guides/Parser-Generator-Guide.md.

Inputs

  • Task (required) ℹ️
    accepts: One of: Fix a failing parser, Create a new parser.
  • Parser (pick a known parser to Fix, or type a new path to Create) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: A known parser (pick from the list) or a new parse_<format>.py path.
  • Tie-out args (Fix only: the parser's CLI args, e.g. 'statement.pdf PASSWORD out.xlsx') (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: Text, e.g. 'statement.pdf PASSWORD out.xlsx'. Optional.
  • Notes (Fix: the symptom / expected closing balance; Create: the format / FORMAT_NAME) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: Text. Fix: the symptom / expected closing balance. Create: the format / FORMAT_NAME. Optional.

How to run

  1. Choose Fix or Create.
  2. Select the parser (or type the new path).
  3. For Fix, provide the tie-out args and the symptom / expected balance in Notes.
  4. Click Run; review the report, and only commit once tie-out exits 0.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-parser-gen/
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-parser-gen/ (a folder)ℹ️ — A report folder with the proposed parser change and the validate / tie-out results. Inspect it before committing the parser.

Tips

The runtime stays deterministic — this tool only edits the format-specific blanks of a parser; the balance oracle and exit contract are never touched.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Run errors mentioning the endpoint / model.This dev tool uses an LLM. Start Ollama or set an endpoint in Settings.
Tie-out still exits non-zero.Add the expected closing balance to Notes and re-run; if it persists, the format may need a manual template tweak.

Partner Compensation Reconciliation offline · no LLM direct

Takes one financial year's partner-compensation documents -- the monthly payout advices, the Compensation Advisory letter, and optionally the LLP's own capital-account statement, a GnuCash book (read only), and a 26AS workbook -- and cross-checks the figures they carry against each other. Every rate, percentage and period this skill uses (the firm's-tax rate, the capital-contribution rate, the capital accretion period, the remuneration-TDS section/rate/start-date) comes from that year's own entity/tax-rules config, never hardcoded, since all of them change by year and the capital rate has been known to change mid-year. A missing rate or a missing source figure produces an explicit "cannot reconcile" row naming what is missing, never a default or a silently-assumed match. The two required documents (the monthly advices and the Advisory) now parse for real; a document that fails to open/parse (unreadable/malformed PDF, wrong password, or content that doesn't match the expected layout) still fails the whole run loud, naming the document and the reason. Every optional document's leg (the LLP statement, the GnuCash books tie-out, the 26AS TDS-credit tie-out) degrades to an explicit "not available" note when its input is absent or cannot yet be parsed. The LLP statement now also parses for real -- its own module docstring names its content-dispatch markers as unverified assumptions, since no real specimen of that document was available (see AGENT.md); the GnuCash books and 26AS tie-outs remain Stage 2 placeholders pending real specimens of those. Parsing the required documents (and the LLP statement, when supplied) successfully does not yet assemble a workbook; that remaining wiring is a further stage, out of this build's scope.

When to use it. Use this once a financial year's partner-compensation documents are in hand and you want a single reconciliation across remuneration, share of profit, the incentive cohort ledger, capital contribution, one-offs, and (if relevant) a payroll stint -- particularly useful for catching a mid-year capital-rate change (which shows up as unequal capital-deducted amounts within one incentive cohort) or a one-off incentive that was grossed up at the wrong year's tax rate. Not a substitute for tax computation or return preparation -- it only reconciles the streams against each other and the return's own figures; it does not compute tax due.

Inputs

  • Monthly partner payout certificates / payslips (required) ℹ️
    accepts: One or more PDF files.
  • Entity (required) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  • Document password (optional -- if the advices/advisory PDFs are protected) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: The PDFs' own open password, if any.
  • Compensation advisory / target compensation advice (required) ℹ️
    accepts: A single PDF file.
  • LLP statement of account (enables leg 1, the capital sign-off) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: A single PDF file.
  • GnuCash book (READ ONLY -- enables the books tie-out) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: GnuCash XML book (.gnucash), optionally gzip-compressed.
  • 26AS workbook (enables the TDS-credit tie-out) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: Excel (.xlsx) with a Part I (TDS) sheet.
  • GnuCash journal CSV output path (optional -- Stage 1b) (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: A full output file path ending in .csv.

How to run

  1. Pick the entity.
  2. Pick this financial year's monthly payout advices (one or more PDFs) and the Compensation Advisory letter.
  3. Optionally supply the LLP statement, a GnuCash book, and/or a 26AS workbook to enable their tie-out legs.
  4. Click Run.
  5. Download the workbook and review the Reconciliation and Exceptions sheets first, then Capital for any mid-year rate-change warning.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-partner-comp-recon.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-partner-comp-recon.xlsxℹ️ — Ten sheets: Logic (the seven reconciled legs and the governing identity, in prose), Drivers (every rate/period/date as a labelled input cell -- the only sheet where one appears as a literal), Monthly grid, Payroll stream (only present if the input supplied payroll months), One-offs (the gross-up and its roundness check), Cohorts (the incentive ledger with its reporting/prior/future FY-assignment column), Capital (the rule as a formula off Drivers, the Advisory cross-check, and the mid-year rate-change detector), Reconciliation (agree / variance / cannot-reconcile per category), Exceptions (every non-agreeing or non-reconcilable row collected together), and Open items (anything left unresolved and what would close it).
  • <journal_path> (optional -- Stage 1b, only written if journal_path is set)ℹ️ — A GnuCash multi-split journal CSV: one balanced transaction per monthly payout (dated month-end), plus an opening reclassification entry if opening_reclass: was supplied. Import via File > Import > Import Transactions from CSV with Multi-split ticked, skipping the 1 header line, Date mapped as ISO, and the Amount column mapped to the importer's Amount column type.

Tips

Start with the Reconciliation sheet, then Exceptions -- a "CANNOT RECONCILE" status names exactly which source figure for that category was not supplied, so a "cannot reconcile" row is something to fix in the input, not a defect in the workbook. On Capital, a "RATE CHANGE SUSPECTED" row means the incentive cohort's instalments show unequal capital-deducted amounts -- re-read that year's Compensation Advisory, since it will have been reissued at a new rate part-way through the cohort.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
A category shows 'CANNOT RECONCILE' with a reason naming a driver or a figure.That figure isn't available for this financial year -- this skill never guesses or falls back to a prior year's value.
Reconciliation shows VARIANCE on the incentive schedule leg.This build has no independent payment-schedule-PDF parser yet (see AGENT.md's Stage 2 note) -- that leg is reported CANNOT RECONCILE rather than VARIANCE for this reason; a VARIANCE elsewhere means two supplied figures genuinely disagree, check the Note column for the exact numbers.
'ERROR: could not parse ...' naming the advisory letter or a payout advice.The PDF is unreadable/malformed, password-protected without the right password, or its content doesn't match the expected layout (e.g. an L1 payout certificate misfiled as the Advisory) -- fix the underlying document/password, not the filename.
The capital sign-off leg (leg 1) shows 'not available' even though llp_statement was supplied.The LLP statement parser dispatches on CONTENT, never filename: 'not available' here means the PDF was unreadable/malformed, password-protected without the right password, or its content didn't match the expected CAPITAL account / CURRENT account layout (e.g. a payout advice or the Advisory letter misfiled as the LLP statement). It never means the leg silently defaulted to zero. This leg is OPTIONAL, so this never fails the whole run -- fix the underlying document/password and re-run. Note the parser's block-header and financial-year wording were written from the task's prose only, with no real specimen read (see llp_statement.py's own ASSUMPTIONS paragraph and AGENT.md); if a real statement uses different wording than assumed, that is the first place to check.

Reconcile offline · no LLM direct

Part II of the KR Choksey → GnuCash flow. Matches the contract notes (SLBM memos and trade notes) against the Part I Simplified Ledger and produces a "Bills" workbook. Runs fully offline (deterministic, no LLM).

When to use it. Run this second, after "Convert" (Part I). Its Bills workbook is the input to "Convert to GnuCash" (Part III).

Inputs

  • Part I Simplified Ledger workbook (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Excel (.xlsx) matching *-KRC-Ledger.xlsx.
  • Contract Notes (SLBM memos + trade notes) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: PDF (.pdf) — one or many contract notes.
  • PDF password (account holder's PAN) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Text — the account holder's PAN.

How to run

  1. Pick the Part I Simplified Ledger from the dropdown.
  2. Select all the contract-note PDFs.
  3. Enter the PDF password (PAN).
  4. Click Run and download the Bills workbook.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-KRC-Bills-Recon.xlsx
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-KRC-Bills-Recon.xlsxℹ️ — The reconciled Bills workbook tying contract notes to the ledger. This is the file you pick in the Convert to GnuCash (Part III) tab.

Tips

A complete set of contract notes is what makes Part II tie out — missing notes show up as unmatched bills.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Some bills are unmatched.A contract note is probably missing for the period. Add it and re-run.
PDF won't open.Check the PAN password and that qpdf is available in source mode.

Skill Scaffolder offline · no LLM direct

Scaffolds a brand-new skill package under src/agents/ -- skill.yaml (a complete manifest with a full help: block), an agent.py stub, an AGENT.md, and a starter test module under tests/ -- entirely by plain text-template substitution. There is no LLM anywhere in the generation path and no network access, so the same inputs always render the exact same bytes. Every piece of prose in the generated files (descriptions, tooltips, steps, troubleshooting, the AGENT.md body) is a fixed placeholder marker rather than invented-sounding text -- a repo-wide guard test fails loudly if a scaffolded skill ever ships with that marker still in it, so a half-finished skill can never slip through silently.

When to use it. Use this to start a new skill instead of hand-copying an existing package. It gets the manifest shape, the help: block structure, and the starter test right on the first try, then leaves clearly marked gaps for a human (or an LLM working under review) to fill in with the real behaviour.

Inputs

  • New package directory name (e.g. skill_foo -- must start with skill_, lowercase) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Must start with skill_ and contain only lowercase letters, digits and underscores after that.
  • Display name for the new skill's UI tab (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Any non-blank text.
  • Category for the new skill (required) ℹ️
    accepts: One of the categories already used elsewhere in this repo.
  • Mode for the new skill (direct = plain function, agent = LLM-driven) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: direct or agent.
  • Output type for the new skill (file or directory) (required) ℹ️
    accepts: file or directory.
  • Does the new skill need an LLM endpoint? (required) ℹ️
    accepts: no or yes.

How to run

  1. Fill in skill_dir, display_name, category, mode, output_type and needs_llm.
  2. Click Run -- it writes the new package under src/agents/ and a starter test under tests/, then runs scripts/gen_docs.py and reports its exit code.
  3. Restart the app -- the new tab only appears after a restart, since the skill registry caches its scan for the life of the process.
  4. Open the new skill's files and replace every placeholder marker with the real implementation, description, and help text before it ships.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-skill-scaffold/
  • skill-scaffold-report.mdℹ️ — Lists exactly which files were created, the gen_docs.py exit code, and the restart reminder.

Tips

Run the full test suite after filling in the placeholders -- the scaffolded test module and the repo-wide help-coverage/marker-guard tests will tell you exactly what is still incomplete.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
"Refused: ... already exists".Pick a different skill_dir -- this tool never overwrites or merges into an existing skill package.
"Refused: skill_dir ... is invalid".skill_dir must match skill_[a-z0-9_]+ -- lowercase, starting with skill_, no path separators.
The new tab doesn't show up after Run.Expected -- restart the app. The skill registry only rescans agents/ once per process.
"Error: the Skill Scaffolder is a source-checkout-only dev tool ...".You're running a frozen/packaged build. Run this from a source checkout instead -- the shipped app's agents/ tree is read-only.

Text Translator needs LLM endpoint direct

Translates text between languages using your configured LLM, and saves the translation as a text file.

When to use it. Use this for quick text translation. Pick 'auto' as the source language to let the model detect it.

Inputs

  • Text to translate (required) ℹ️
    accepts: Free text.
  • Source language (optional) ℹ️
    accepts: auto, English, Hindi, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, Portuguese, Russian.
  • Target language (required) ℹ️
    accepts: English, Hindi, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, Portuguese, Russian.

How to run

  1. Paste the text.
  2. Set source (or 'auto') and target language.
  3. Click Run and download the translation.

Output

Written to Data/outputs/:

Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-translation.txt
  • YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-translation.txtℹ️ — The translated text in the target language.

Tips

Translation quality depends on the model you have connected — a larger model generally handles nuance and less-common languages better.

Troubleshooting

If…Then…
Run errors mentioning the endpoint / model.This skill needs an LLM. Start Ollama or set an endpoint in Settings.
Output mixes languages or is off.Set the source language explicitly instead of 'auto', or try a larger model.
